message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait/efo and phenotyping_reported align to abdominal aortic aneurysm). Two are from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet; PGS003972/PGS003973) with broad multi-cohort development, which domain guidance favors over framework/portability scores when endpoint is the same. Between those siblings, PGS003972 is preferred because it is the cleaner PRS-oriented evaluation record: full-model AUROC=0.69 without disclosed covariates (unknown, but not explicitly risk-wrapper packaging), whereas PGS003973 reports a very high C-index=0.882 in a model explicitly adjusted for age/age^2/sex, suggesting the discrimination is likely covariate-driven and not directly comparable as PRS performance. Framework alternatives (PGS001784 global biobank; PGS002054 UKB portability) have PRS-comparable metrics (R2/partial-r ~0.014–0.0144) and much larger validation, but are penalized by their pan-trait/portability archetype versus the disease-focused Nat Genet family. Confidence is limited because the selected model lacks explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2/effect-size reporting and uses an 'Unknown' covariate set, while other candidates provide clearer PRS-only metrics or effect sizes."}

Among them, PGS003972 (PRS-CS; Nat Genet 2023 AAA GWAS meta-analysis) is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused, multi-cohort development set (many AAA-relevant cohorts listed) rather than a pan-trait/framework/portability context (PGS001784: “Global Biobank analyses…”; PGS002054: “Portability of 245 polygenic scores…”). Its reported discrimination in European evaluation (AUROC=0.69) is within-range and avoids relying on an unusually high full-model metric. Main limitation: performance reporting is incomplete/heterogeneous across candidates (several have only full-model AUROC/C-index or partial-r, many lack PRS-only AUROC/incremental metrics; covariates are unknown for some), and PGS003973 shows a much higher C-index (0.882) but with time-to-event style metric and unclear PRS-only contribution, making it hard to compare directly—so confidence remains moderate and outcome is sub-optimal rather than high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo align to abdominal aortic aneurysm; phenotyping_reported is AAA for all, with PGS000753 noted as prevalent AAA). Prioritizing disease-focused multi-cohort development over pan-trait/framework scores per provided domain policy favors the Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis–derived scores (PGS003972/PGS003973) over the Global Biobank framework score (PGS001784) and the UKB portability score (PGS002054), despite those having explicit PRS-side R2/partial-r. Between the Nat Genet siblings, PGS003972 has broader listed development cohorts (includes UKB and VIVA in addition to ARIC/HUNT/MVP/deCODE/eMERGE, etc.) and more validation records (record_count=3 vs 1), while reported full-model discrimination is not clearly PRS-only for either (AUROC=0.69 for PGS003972; C-index=0.882 for PGS003973 but with no PRS-only/incremental metric and thus likely covariate-influenced by age/sex). {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches to abdominal aortic aneurysm by trait/EFO and (where provided) phenotyping. Two candidates (PGS003972/PGS003973; Nat Genet 2023 AAA GWAS meta-analysis) have the strongest disease-focused multi-cohort development context (many AAA-relevant cohorts) and provide reported discrimination in European evaluation, which is preferable to the pan-trait/framework-style origins of PGS001784 (Global Biobank PRS lessons) and PGS002054 (UKB portability paper), and to the older sparse P+T model PGS000753. Between the Nat Genet siblings, PGS003973 reports a high full-model C-index (0.882) with basic covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex) but lacks PRS-only metrics; PGS003972 reports a lower full-model AUROC (0.69). Given domain guidance not to over-rank on full-model metrics alone (and that the 0.882 may be largely covariate-driven), PGS003972 is selected as the more conservative representative of the disease-focused study family without relying on an outlier full-model C-index. Limitation: across candidates, PRS-only AUROC/incremental metrics are largely missing, covariates are unknown for some, and the key tie between the Nat Genet siblings cannot be cleanly resolved from the provided metadata, so confidence is not high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have phenotype-aligned endpoints (mostly generic AAA; PGS000753 is explicitly prevalent AAA). By the domain-knowledge policy for cardiovascular/large-vessel disease, a disease-focused multi-cohort/meta-analysis score with basic demographic covariates is generally preferred over older sparse prevalent-endpoint models; however, the Nat Genet siblings have limitations in the visible metadata: their reported discrimination is full-model (AUROC/C-index) rather than PRS-only, covariates are unknown for PGS003972, and the very high C-index for PGS003973 is not directly comparable as PRS performance. Remaining limitation: performance reporting is heterogeneous across candidates (mostly full-model metrics or partial-r), and the disease-focused Nat Genet family cannot be cleanly ranked versus PGS000753 using PRS-comparable metrics from the provided context, so the recommendation is not high-confidence."}
